director.chapterArc: Jab moves from wary estrangement into brief social reconnection, then converts worsening evidence about Tonk into a hard deadline. The carter offers the safe, humane answer; Jab rejects it because its single flaw is tomorrow. Practical kindness equips him for the dangerous final mile. The blade and Tonk’s recognition of the silent song create a small pocket of intimacy before the closing reversal: an unseen follower stops when Jab does not.
director.restraintNote: Keep Jab’s flatness purposeful: it is a method for obtaining an answer while suppressing panic, not emotional vacancy. Treat infection, magic, and hounds as physical facts. Let humor release pressure briefly; let grief surface through arithmetic, useful objects, and action. The blade is a failing tool, not a spectacle. Preserve warmth in the final exchange without sentimentalizing it, then make the last threat quiet and spatially exact.

cues.delivery: Answer with practical patience; let his concealed relief at Tonk’s wakefulness warm the narration without admitting the fear beneath it.
cues.from: "I said today. It's today. I didn't say now."
cues.through: Tonk made a sound that meant the distinction was noted and rejected. He had been awake since first light, which was more than he had managed in four days, and Jab had spent the first hour of it so glad that he had not looked at why.
cues.reason: Tonk’s alertness briefly restores ordinary brotherly rhythm while Jab avoids examining its cause.

cues.delivery: Land Tonk’s negotiation with dry adult formality, then allow Jab’s laugh to loosen only a fraction of his social dread.
cues.from: "Say hello to one," Tonk said, with the air of a man making a fair offer, and Jab, who had been dreading the next person on the road for the last quarter of an hour, laughed and found that he had stopped dreading them quite so much.
cues.through: "Say hello to one," Tonk said, with the air of a man making a fair offer, and Jab, who had been dreading the next person on the road for the last quarter of an hour, laughed and found that he had stopped dreading them quite so much.
cues.reason: This is the chapter’s first clean pressure release.

cues.delivery: Read the wound assessment clinically and without disgust; let the matching heat supply the dread by itself.
cues.from: The open place low on the outside had widened. There was less to see than there had been, and more to smell, and the skin all round it had gone a dull colour that was not the angry colour it had been for a fortnight. He put the back of his hand on the shin above it and then on the boy's forehead and got the same heat off both.
cues.through: The open place low on the outside had widened. There was less to see than there had been, and more to smell, and the skin all round it had gone a dull colour that was not the angry colour it had been for a fortnight. He put the back of his hand on the shin above it and then on the boy's forehead and got the same heat off both.
cues.reason: The infection’s acceleration becomes physically undeniable.

cues.delivery: Let the laughter become an involuntary pressure leak, not sobbing; recover control on the sleeve and the turn away.
cues.from: Jab sat in the dry grass beside a stone wall with his brother's whole chest going up and down too fast under a hide, and laughed until his eyes ran, and then wiped his face with his sleeve before he turned round.
cues.through: Jab sat in the dry grass beside a stone wall with his brother's whole chest going up and down too fast under a hide, and laughed until his eyes ran, and then wiped his face with his sleeve before he turned round.
cues.reason: Jab’s restraint briefly fails under Tonk’s clear-eyed joke.

cues.delivery: Make the stranger’s familiar sound catch Jab off guard; keep the recognition small, bodily, and immediately contained.
cues.from: "Hm," said the carter, in a way that made the hair go up on Jab's arms, because it was his father's noise exactly, made by a stranger on a road four hundred miles from anywhere his father had ever stood.
cues.through: "Hm," said the carter, in a way that made the hair go up on Jab's arms, because it was his father's noise exactly, made by a stranger on a road four hundred miles from anywhere his father had ever stood.
cues.reason: A trace of home reaches him through the carter.

cues.delivery: Give the carter plain, unsentimental generosity; he has already done the arithmetic and presents shelter as logistics, not charity.
cues.from: "I'm going to the north yard," he said. "I go in the morning. I've a shed at the turn, about a mile on, and a stove in it, and I'll be at that gate at the second hour after light with the boy on the cart and you walking beside him, and it'll cost you nothing because there's nothing you've got."
cues.through: "I'm going to the north yard," he said. "I go in the morning. I've a shed at the turn, about a mile on, and a stove in it, and I'll be at that gate at the second hour after light with the boy on the cart and you walking beside him, and it'll cost you nothing because there's nothing you've got."
cues.reason: The offer creates a credible safe alternative.

cues.delivery: State the hounds’ behavior like a known road hazard; underplay the final conditional so its uncertainty becomes the menace.
cues.from: "Whatever's coming through this month." The carter shrugged. "Hounds, mostly, this time of year. They lie up in the ditches and they count you. If you're lucky they count you and go."
cues.through: "Whatever's coming through this month." The carter shrugged. "Hounds, mostly, this time of year. They lie up in the ditches and they count you. If you're lucky they count you and go."
cues.reason: The external danger receives its clearest rule.

cues.delivery: Let the stranger’s blunt question make the truth usable. Build the shelter vision with exhausted longing, then land “tomorrow” without pleading or emphasis beyond the final recognition.
cues.from: And there it was, laid out flat on the grass between them by a man who had known him for four minutes, which was a thing Jab had not been able to do for himself in four days.
cues.through: Everything about it was right, and he could see it all, and it had exactly one thing wrong with it, which was that it was tomorrow.
cues.reason: The safe plan is fully imagined and rejected because it arrives too late.

cues.delivery: Count each fact with disciplined clarity; make the date the inevitable result of the sum, not a dramatic pronouncement.
cues.from: And under that, not from the thing in his chest at all but from the ordinary part of him that had been counting fish and twists and rests for sixteen days, came the rest of the arithmetic. Three twists. A fever with no top on it. A smell that had changed this morning and not last week. The Elder at a table with her hands flat on it, saying six weeks to a room, in front of people who had argued with her and lost.
cues.reason: Jab calculates that Tonk has reached the predicted limit.

cues.delivery: Speak with complete honesty and no bid for sympathy; the unbearable future is the mile remembered, not death named aloud.
cues.from: "It's a real sum," he said. "The other one's in there. I know it's in there. But if I sit in your shed tonight and he turns, I'll have the whole of the rest of my life to think about the mile."
cues.through: "It's a real sum," he said. "The other one's in there. I know it's in there. But if I sit in your shed tonight and he turns, I'll have the whole of the rest of my life to think about the mile."
cues.reason: Jab reveals the personal cost driving his otherwise rational decision.

cues.delivery: Let the carter reclaim agency with dry irritation; kindness stays disguised as a practical right he has earned.
cues.from: "Right," he said, and turned round and started untying one of his sacks, which was not what Jab had braced for at all. "Then you'll take this, and you'll not argue with me about it, because I've stood here and failed to talk you into a stove and I'm going to be allowed to do something."
cues.through: "Right," he said, and turned round and started untying one of his sacks, which was not what Jab had braced for at all. "Then you'll take this, and you'll not argue with me about it, because I've stood here and failed to talk you into a stove and I'm going to be allowed to do something."
cues.reason: The refused shelter reverses into useful aid.

cues.delivery: Deliver the instructions as hard-won procedural knowledge. Keep every repeated phrase distinct and useful, with no inspirational warmth.
cues.from: "No," the carter agreed. "You can't. You'll do me a favour instead and it's this: when you get to that gate you'll say the word clinical before they've got your boots off, and then you'll say it again, and then — this is the part I want — when they tell you you can't come in, you'll ask them who you talk to, and you'll keep asking that same question at every person they hand you to. Not let me in. Who do I talk to. They've got an answer to that one and they haven't got an answer to the other one, and the difference is about a day."
cues.through: "No," the carter agreed. "You can't. You'll do me a favour instead and it's this: when you get to that gate you'll say the word clinical before they've got your boots off, and then you'll say it again, and then — this is the part I want — when they tell you you can't come in, you'll ask them who you talk to, and you'll keep asking that same question at every person they hand you to. Not let me in. Who do I talk to. They've got an answer to that one and they haven't got an answer to the other one, and the difference is about a day."
cues.reason: The carter gives Jab a tactic that may save a day.

cues.delivery: Let the broken chair explain the generosity without softening the carter’s reserve; turn the final warning back into brisk roadcraft.
cues.from: "Because I had a girl with a bad hip," he said, "and I've had the chair on this cart for nine years and I've never once got round to mending the arm of it." He clicked his tongue at the pony. "Go on, then. Go fast and don't stop in the sag, and if something stands still and looks at you, don't you stand still and look back."
cues.through: "Because I had a girl with a bad hip," he said, "and I've had the chair on this cart for nine years and I've never once got round to mending the arm of it." He clicked his tongue at the pony. "Go on, then. Go fast and don't stop in the sag, and if something stands still and looks at you, don't you stand still and look back."
cues.reason: The carter’s private loss surfaces once, then becomes protection.

cues.delivery: Make the request steady but too immediate to hide its need; Jab is checking for consciousness while pretending to invite conversation.
Give Tonk a thin, distant clarity; keep Jab’s discovery of the rigid little fist tactile and silent.
cues.from: "Little's cold," Tonk said, from a long way down, and Jab put his hand back over his own shoulder and felt for the small fist and found the wooden fish still in it, held so hard that the fingers had gone stiff around it.
cues.through: "Little's cold," Tonk said, from a long way down, and Jab put his hand back over his own shoulder and felt for the small fist and found the wooden fish still in it, held so hard that the fingers had gone stiff around it.
cues.reason: Tonk’s delirious answer reveals both fever and continued attachment to the fish.

cues.delivery: Hold the blade where Tonk can see it as a wordless reassurance; keep the image grounded in weight, road, and walking.
cues.from: Jab held it out a little to the side, where his brother could see the whole of it, and walked on down the middle of a straight road with an amber line burning on his fist and a boy watching it over his shoulder.
cues.through: Jab held it out a little to the side, where his brother could see the whole of it, and walked on down the middle of a straight road with an amber line burning on his fist and a boy watching it over his shoulder.
cues.reason: Jab turns a costly tool into comfort for his brother.

cues.delivery: Let Tonk’s correction arrive with faint childish precision; the tenderness comes from his noticing, not from a comic flourish.
cues.from: "No," said Tonk. "You. You're doing the boat one. With your mouth shut."
cues.through: "No," said Tonk. "You. You're doing the boat one. With your mouth shut."
cues.reason: A moment of lucid recognition interrupts the decline.

cues.delivery: Sing through the prose rather than performing the song: open the voice slightly, but let the empty fields swallow it without consolation.
cues.from: So he sang it out loud instead, all four verses he had left, on an empty road at the front edge of a winter night, and his voice went out flat across the black fields either side and came back off nothing at all.
cues.through: So he sang it out loud instead, all four verses he had left, on an empty road at the front edge of a winter night, and his voice went out flat across the black fields either side and came back off nothing at all.
cues.reason: Jab answers Tonk with the last verses he remembers.

cues.delivery: Begin as a quiet continuation of the song, then sharpen the spatial facts—third verse, left ditch, amber edge—and stop cleanly on “stopped.”
cues.from: And somewhere in the third verse, out in the ditch on the left, at the edge of what the amber line could show him, something that had been keeping station with him stopped.
cues.through: And somewhere in the third verse, out in the ditch on the left, at the edge of what the amber line could show him, something that had been keeping station with him stopped.
cues.reason: The intimate lull reverses into immediate external threat.
